> [@joaomj](https://github.com/joaomj) sorry, I missed your earlier question before adding this measurement.
> 
> No: my config does not explicitly set `"snapshot": false`, so this evidence does not establish behavior under that setting. Current source shows the `snapshot` option gating session Git snapshot/diff generation in `packages/opencode/src/session/summary.ts`; the database growth discussed here is retained `message.updated.1` / `message.part.updated.1` event history. I therefore would not expect that option to disable these event writes, but that is a source-based expectation rather than a controlled measurement. A useful follow-up would compare event-row and byte growth for the same output-heavy workload with snapshot enabled versus disabled.
> 
> Additional long-lived macOS instance evidence: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` reached 64 GiB. A direct `dbstat` attribution query could not complete within 120 seconds under normal runtime load, so even diagnosis was operationally expensive. The sibling tool-output store separately reached 33 GiB ([#29694](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/29694)). This strengthens the need for bounded built-in storage stats, event retention/compaction, and an idle-safe checkpoint/VACUUM workflow before the database reaches tens of GiB.

I can reproduce the overwrite by calling `ProviderTransform.message()` twice on the same already-normalized message, but I haven’t found a production path that does that. The transform runs only while building an outgoing request; the next OpenCode step rebuilds messages from persisted response parts, and that path already preserves the reasoning part / `reasoning_content` without this change. AI SDK `streamText` also defaults to a single step here (`stopWhen = stepCountIs(1)`), so it does not appear to feed the transformed request back through the middleware internally.

A test demonstrating where the previously normalized message re-enters `ProviderTransform.message()` would clarify the bug and ensure this change covers the reported failure.

One specific concern with the description: OpenCode does not persist the output of `ProviderTransform.message()`. It persists provider response parts. On the next step, `MessageV2.toModelMessages()` reconstructs the reasoning part (including its provider metadata), and `normalizeMessages()` extracts the reasoning text again.

I tested that persistence/reconstruction path without this PR using a stored assistant reasoning part plus tool call; the next outgoing request retained the non-empty `reasoning_content`. The empty overwrite occurred only when I explicitly passed the already-normalized output through `ProviderTransform.message()` a second time.

If there is a separate path where persistence or reconstruction drops the reasoning part but retains message-level `providerOptions`, please include that shape/path in the reproduction. As written, the DB explanation does not appear to match the current storage flow.

Confirming this reproduces on v1.18.5 (macOS, `opencode serve` + web UI).

Concrete example from a real session — one user message produced two
terminal assistant siblings:

| message | ID prefix | time_created | input | cache.read |
|---------|-----------|--------------|-------|------------|
| user | `msg_faf2259**52**001…` | +0 ms | — | — |
| assistant #1 | `msg_faf2259**4f**001…` | +103 ms | 63 780 | 13 312 |
| assistant #2 | `msg_faf231fc4…` | +51 s | 2 647 | 76 800 |

The assistant ID sorts lexicographically *before* the user ID (`4f < 52`)
despite being created 103 ms later, so `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id`
evaluates false and the loop re-enters. The second call has the classic
tiny-input / huge-cache-read signature.

Downstream effect: the model sees its own first answer in context and
hallucinates it as user input, producing confused follow-ups.

This matches the 2.8% collision rate documented in #28986. The fix is
correct and minimal. Would appreciate a maintainer review — this has been
open across 5+ duplicate issues and 4 PRs since February without a merge.

Maintainers please react to it!

Same pattern as described in the issue — a tool call executes successfully (confirmed via git diff, real correct edits land on disk), but the session ends with no final assistant message. Log shows the loop advancing and exiting immediately after the tool round, with no second stream call and no error:

timestamp=...T18:57:30.836Z level=INFO message=stream providerID=mtplx modelID=gemma4-mtplx-optimized-speed ... agent=build mode=primary
timestamp=...T18:58:18.550Z level=INFO message=tracking hash=... (file change tracked)
timestamp=...T18:58:18.570Z level=INFO message=loop session.id=... step=2
timestamp=...T18:58:18.570Z level=INFO message="exiting loop" session.id=...

This matches the root cause described above — the loop-exit check only looks at finish_reason against ["tool-calls", "unknown"], so any provider that returns "stop" on a turn that actually contained tool calls will silently truncate the session. Given it's now confirmed across Gemini, LiteLLM, and MTPLX, this seems like a fairly broad compatibility gap rather than a single-provider quirk — might be worth having the loop check for the presence of tool calls in the response directly, rather than trusting the provider's finish_reason string.

Hit this in the field today: managed server restarted mid-run, parent and child were resumed independently, and `settleStaleToolCalls` (`packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts`) marked the in-flight `subagent` tool part aborted. The model saw a failed tool and retried, spawning a second child while the original was still resumable. So the foreground case also has a duplicate provider spend failure mode, not just a lost result.

Proposed implementation plan:

1. **Durable invocation event, not a durable Job.** Record one `session.subagent.invoked` event on the parent (child session ID, parent tool-call ID, mode, description) in the same transaction that creates the child, projected into a small `subagent_invocation` table with a delivery state (`pending` -> `delivered`/`aborted`). The invocation is the irreducible new fact; the table is a rebuildable fold cache. The child outcome is already durable in its own session history, so nothing is persisted twice. `Job.Service` stays process-local as documented.

2. **State-driven delivery instead of a forked waiter.** Delivery is derivable at any time: child session terminal + invocation delivery pending -> admit the synthetic completion. The in-process fiber in `notifyWhenDone` becomes an optimization over the same code path, and a startup reconciler is that code path run once at boot. Admit the completion with a deterministic message ID derived from the child session ID, so the existing prompt-ID reconciliation rules make duplicate reconcilers and restart races collapse to exactly one wake.

3. **Teach `settleStaleToolCalls` to consult the invocation table.** Before aborting a stale `subagent` tool part: child still running or suspended -> do not abort, settle the call as demoted-to-background ("still running, you will be notified") and let the background delivery path handle completion; child already terminal -> settle from the child's final assistant text; no invocation or child gone -> abort as today. This kills the abort -> model retries -> orphan duplicate child loop.

4. **Cascades through the durable record.** Parent tool interrupt -> interrupt child (exists today, route it through the record so it works cross-restart). Child deleted -> invocation settles aborted.

On the foreground question in the issue: true reattach (re-entering a blocked tool call in the resumed parent runner) is new machinery. Demoting the recovered foreground call to background semantics reuses the delivery path from step 2 and satisfies "must not silently become an unrelated orphan child". I would start there and only build real reattach if the UX demands it.

Suggested order: 1+2 first (background subagents silently vanishing is the worst case, the model was promised a notification that never arrives), then 3, then the restart test matrix from the issue body.

Attaching a ready-to-apply patch implementing the proposed fix, in case it's useful before a PR is up. Apply with:

```bash
git am < plugin-serverurl-inprocess.patch
```

Summary of the change (in `packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts`):
- `baseUrl` fallback: `"http://localhost:4096"` → `"http://opencode.internal"`
- `serverUrl` getter fallback: `new URL("http://localhost:4096")` → `new URL("http://opencode.internal")`

Behavior-neutral for the plugin client (the in-process transport routes via `Server.Default().app.fetch` regardless of `baseUrl` host); it only makes the reported `serverUrl` honest so plugins can detect there's no external TCP server.

<details>
<summary>plugin-serverurl-inprocess.patch</summary>

```diff
From 6659527c98a067691684a188c292434f215eb690 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Robert Gillin <rgillin@legalzoom.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 13:16:53 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] fix(plugin): report in-process placeholder in serverUrl when
 no HTTP listener is bound

When the TUI runs with the default in-process transport (no --port/--hostname/--mdns),
Server.url is undefined and PluginInput.serverUrl fell back to a fabricated
http://localhost:4096, implying a reachable TCP server that does not exist. Plugins
that dial ctx.serverUrl (e.g. cmux subagent-viewer's 'opencode attach') silently fail.

Report the in-process placeholder http://opencode.internal instead, matching tui.ts
and run.ts, so plugins can detect there is no external server. The in-process client
routes via Server.Default().app.fetch regardless of baseUrl host, so this is
behavior-neutral for the plugin client and only makes the reported URL honest.
---
 packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts | 11 +++++++++--
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts b/packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts
index 1558c70..2b0a895 100644
--- a/packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts
+++ b/packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts
@@ -139,8 +139,12 @@ const layer = Layer.effect(
         const { Server } = yield* Effect.promise(() => import("../server/server"))
 
         const serverUrl = Server.url
+        // When no HTTP listener is bound (the default in-process TUI transport),
+        // there is no reachable loopback URL. Report the in-process placeholder
+        // ("http://opencode.internal") rather than a fabricated localhost:4096,
+        // which would falsely imply a live TCP server that plugins can dial.
         const client = createOpencodeClient({
-          baseUrl: serverUrl?.toString() ?? "http://localhost:4096",
+          baseUrl: serverUrl?.toString() ?? "http://opencode.internal",
           directory: ctx.directory,
           headers: ServerAuth.headers(),
           ...(serverUrl ? {} : { fetch: async (...args) => Server.Default().app.fetch(...args) }),
@@ -157,7 +161,10 @@ const layer = Layer.effect(
             },
           },
           get serverUrl(): URL {
-            return Server.url ?? new URL("http://localhost:4096")
+            // Reflect the bound listener when one exists; otherwise surface the
+            // in-process placeholder so plugins can detect there is no external
+            // TCP server instead of being handed a dead localhost:4096 URL.
+            return Server.url ?? new URL("http://opencode.internal")
           },
           // @ts-expect-error
           $: typeof Bun === "undefined" ? undefined : Bun.$,
-- 
2.50.1 (Apple Git-155)

```
</details>

The `process.exit()` explanation in this thread doesn't hold up. Removing the `process.exit()` from `src/index.ts` entirely and waiting 2s still truncated at exactly 65536.

What's actually happening is backpressure. `process.stdout.write()` returns `false` once the pipe buffer is full, and the queued remainder is dropped when the process exits. `console.log` does the same and gives you nothing to await.

That explains why #3049 didn't fix it: it moved `export` to `process.stdout.write` but never waited for the write to be accepted, so the second half of the problem was still there.

It also affects `opencode db` and `opencode session list --format json`, not just `export`. Repro that needs no existing session:

```bash
Q="with recursive t(n) as (select 1 union all select n+1 from t where n < 5000)
   select n as n, '0123456789012345678901234567890123456789' as pad from t"

opencode db --format json "$Q" | wc -c        # 65536
opencode db --format json "$Q" > f; wc -c f   # 388896
```

Exit code is 0 both times. Worth flagging for TSV specifically: truncated output still parses, so a consumer just sees a smaller table and no error.

Opened #39577 with a fix (await drain, EPIPE resolves so `| head` still works).

One separate thing I hit while narrowing this down, which may be a Bun bug rather than ours: `console.log` drops everything past 64 KiB once `@babel/core` is in the module graph, even on a natural exit with no `process.exit()` involved. `packages/opencode/bunfig.toml` preloads `@opentui/solid/preload`, which pulls in Babel.

```bash
bun add @babel/core
echo 'console.log("x".repeat(200000))' > main.ts
echo 'import "@babel/core"' > pre.ts
bun main.ts | wc -c                       # 200001
bun --preload ./pre.ts main.ts | wc -c    # 65536
```

Tested on opencode 1.18.7 and dev, bun 1.3.11, macOS arm64.

lexicographic ID comparison is fundamentally fragile

It assumes.

1. IDs are always ULIDs with embedded timestamps
2. No two messages are created in the same millisecond
3. Compaction doesn't rewrite messages with new IDs
4. Imported sessions use time-sortable IDs

None of these are guaranteed.

Ran a simplification review pass (three parallel reviewers: reuse, quality, efficiency). Applied:

- Restructured the backfill compensation check to remove a logically dead `before === undefined` disjunct (it existed only to narrow the type; now two honest early returns).
- Corrected the streaming-pause comment: appends only reset the backfill timer until the first chunk pins `hiddenRows`; after that backfill drains on a fixed cadence, which reviewers agreed is the better behavior (no timer churn per streaming delta). The comment now says what the code does.
- Deduplicated `dialog.clear()` in `scrollToMessage`.

Declined with reasons: promoting `afterLayout` to a shared util (it is the 4th double-rAF copy in the repo, but migrating dialog-select/diff-viewer belongs in a follow-up, not this PR); Map-keyed `boundaryID` and slice-cost reductions (bounded small at the 200-message cap, already noted in Scope). Checked `@opentui/core` ScrollBox for a public at-bottom accessor: only private `_stickyScrollBottom`, so the manual check stays.

Tests/typecheck unchanged (same single pre-existing flake).

Simplification review pass applied two fixes to the prefetch effect:

- It now tracks only the open-tab id set (sorted, via memo) plus enabled/connection status. Previously it also tracked the current session and tab order, so every tab switch or drag reorder cleared the timer, restarted the warm loop from the first tab, and re-fetched any previously failed sync (failed syncs are evicted from the dedup cache). The current-session filter moved inside the timer callback, which runs untracked.
- Dropped the dead in-loop connection check (a status change reruns the effect, whose cleanup already flags the pass stale before the loop can observe it) and named the magic delay (`TAB_PREFETCH_DELAY = 300`).

Declined: a `data.session.syncAll` bundle in the data context. Reviewers correctly flagged that enumerating the five syncs here duplicates knowledge the session route owns, but centralizing it is a data-context API change, which this PR deliberately avoids; that consolidation belongs to the planned data-layer prefetch/paging design.

All 568 tests pass, typecheck and formatting clean.
